steps.title: Set up your workbench
actions: Choose filament colors, paint or both.
If you paint, keep paint off nut pockets, threads, mating faces and adhesive contact areas.
Let the paint cure for the time on its label before assembly.
Gather the tools in the {tools}.
Sort the screws by size.
Keep each servo’s horn and center screw together.
steps.check: Your colors are chosen, your tools are ready and your screws are sorted.

steps.title: Slice and print the plates
actions: Open the all-plates Bambu project in Bambu Studio.
Select your printer, nozzle and build plate.
Map each plate’s material profile to one of your spools.
Keep the supplied orientations, supports, support blockers and brims.
Leave “Synchronize filament list from AMS” off.
Slice one plate at a time. Start with plate 2, the base.
Inspect the slice before you print it.
When you send a plate to the printer, turn bed leveling on. Turn timelapse off.
For plate 2, turn flow dynamics calibration off. The printer’s calibration line crosses that plate’s front brim.
Print plate 2. Print plate 7 next, the same way. It holds the base’s panels and grilles.
Print the rest in the order the build first needs them: 1, 3, 4, 6, 8, 5, 10 and 9.
The plate layouts above list each plate’s parts and estimate.
steps.check: Plates 2 and 7 are printed with their supplied settings.

panels.title: Print plates 2 and 7 first

steps.title: Clean and check each print
actions: Let each part cool before you remove its supports.
Remove supports and brims in small pieces.
As you work, hold thin fingers, eye housing lips, horn seats, antenna turns, threads and nut-channel ledges from behind.
On the backpack shell (P35), hold the belt tabs while you clear the hinge gaps and lower screw passages.
Clear the P35 pin holes.
In the base (FB01), clear the small support lips from the front nut-entry channels.
Clear the screw holes and cable slots in the base. Clear the nut pockets for the boards, bottom cover, audio cradle, rear vent, button and power jack plate. Clear the side grille nut channels.
Smooth rough edges at the central wire hole. Do not enlarge the hole.
On the audio cradle (FB24), clear the end windows and lid-nut slots.
Clear support from the horn recesses in both upper arms (AR01, AR04).
Test-fit the real screws, nuts and mating parts. Do not force them. Test-fit means fitting parts without glue or final tightening, and removing them afterwards.
Check how the eyes, eye housings and head shelf (P08) fit the head shell (GS20).
Set aside cracked, warped or delaminated parts for reprinting.
steps.check: The base, its grilles and the rear vent are clean. Their screw holes, nut pockets and cable paths are clear.

panels.caption: Front nut-entry channel and its nut, seen from inside the base.

safety.text: The plastic behind the front nuts is thin. Too much force can crack it. Clear the channels without thinning that plastic.

steps.title: Glue the board and cover nuts
actions: Place the empty base (FB01) upside down, with its open bottom facing up.
Seat an M2 nut in the tip of each of the eight board posts. Four are for the Pi and two for each level shifter. Match its flats to the pocket. Do not force it.
With a toothpick, put a tiny dab of mixed epoxy (C09) where each nut’s edge meets its pocket. Or use faster-setting CA gel (C18). Keep glue out of threads and off the post tips.
Seat an M3 nut in the bottom cover recess at each of the four corners. Match its flats to the recess.
Glue each nut at its outside edge, as for the board nuts. Keep glue off the faces where the cover seats.
Leave the base upside down until the glue holds.
steps.check: The eight board nuts and four cover nuts sit flat in their pockets. No glue is in their threads or on the seating faces.

detail.title: Where the eight board nuts go

steps.title: Glue the audio cradle nuts
actions: With the base (FB01) still upside down, find the three open recesses behind the front opening. Drop an M3 nut into each recess. Match its flats to the recess.
Glue each nut at its outside edge with epoxy (C09) or CA gel (C18), as in {step:board-cover-nuts}. The glue holds these nuts while the cradle screws go in.
Each nut sits flat in its recess.
Leave the base upside down. Let the glue cure fully, for the time on its label.
Check gently that every glued nut stays seated. Start a matching screw in each thread by hand. Do not drive it against the plastic.
Remove the test screws. Leave the base empty.
steps.check: All 15 glued nuts (8 M2 and 7 M3) stay seated. Every screw starts freely by hand. The board and cover seating faces are clear.

panels.title: Glue the three audio cradle nuts
Let the glue cure and test each nut

steps.title: Fit the front grille and rear vent
actions: Place the base (FB01) upside down, with its open bottom facing up.
Find the front opening. The front microphone grille (FB41) fits here.
Find the rear opening. The rear vent (FB03) fits here.
Find the four nut channels on the inside of the front wall, around the opening. Place an M3 nut flat against the wall in each channel.
Slide each nut toward the top of the base until it stops. Do not force it. Do not glue these nuts.
Each nut rests at the end of its channel, over its screw hole.
At the front opening, hold the grille against the outside of the base. Put one M3×6 screw through a grille hole. Use no washers.
With your other hand, press that hole’s nut against the wall from inside. Turn the screw by hand until it catches.
Repeat for the other three holes, one screw at a time. Tighten all four screws evenly.
The grille sits flat against the base.
If a screw does not start by hand, remove it. Check that its nut is seated.
Through the open bottom, place an M3 nut in one of the four pockets around the rear opening. Match its flats to the pocket. Hold it there with a fingertip. Do not glue it.
With your other hand, hold the rear vent against the outside of the base. Put an M3×12 screw through the vent into that nut. Use no washer. Turn it by hand until it catches.
Repeat for the other three pockets, one nut at a time. Tighten all four screws evenly. Leave the bottom of the base open.
The vent sits flat against the base.
steps.check: Both parts sit flat. Each nut stays seated and the plastic around it is not cracked.

steps.title: Attach the speakers to their grilles
actions: Place one speaker (E16) against the inside of a loose side speaker grille (FB19). Face its cone toward the grille opening.
Line up the four speaker tabs with the four inner holes of the grille.
From the outside, insert four M3×12 screws through the grille and speaker tabs. On the speaker side, add one M3 washer and one M3 nut to each screw.
Hold each nut while you tighten its screw until snug. Keep the speaker tabs flat.
The speaker sits flat against the grille. Its tabs are not bent.
Repeat for the second speaker. Leave both speaker cables unplugged.
steps.check: Both speakers are held firmly against their grilles. Screw tips clear the speaker housing and cables.
steps.note: You mount these grilles on the base in {step:side-grilles}.

steps.title: Mount the side speaker grilles
actions: Keep the base upside down, with its open bottom facing up. On one side, place an M3 nut flat against the wall in each of the four channels. These nuts take the grille’s outer holes.
Slide each nut toward the top of the base until it stops. Do not force it. Do not glue these nuts.
Each nut rests at the end of its channel, over its screw hole.
Pass the speaker cable through the side opening. Keep the cable clear of the mounting edge.
Hold the side speaker grille (FB19) flat against the outside of the base. Put one M3×12 screw through an outer hole. Use no washers.
With your other hand, press that hole’s nut against the wall from inside. Turn the screw by hand until it catches.
Repeat for the other three outer holes. Tighten the four screws evenly.
The grille sits flat against the base.
Repeat panels 1 to 3 on the other side.
Label each speaker cable with its side: robot-left or robot-right.
Leave enough cable slack to pull a grille away for service.
Leave the plugs disconnected until {step:audio-module}.
steps.check: Both grilles sit flat. The speakers and cables are inside the base, with no cable pinched under an edge.
steps.note: You attached the speakers to these grilles in {step:speaker-grilles}.

steps.title: Fit the feet
actions: Keep the base (FB01) upside down, with its open bottom facing up.
Choose four matching adhesive feet (E25) that fit on the base’s Ø14 mm post faces.
Clean and dry the four post faces.
Peel the backing from one foot. Center it on a post face. Press it on firmly. Repeat for the other three feet.
Let the adhesive bond for the time on its label before you load the feet.
Stand the base upright. Check that it does not rock.
steps.check: The base stands level on four firmly bonded feet.

steps.title: Set up your computer and SSH key
actions: If you use Windows, install WSL first. Run every terminal command in this guide in WSL, including key creation, cloning and Make. Run Imager in Windows.
On your computer, install Git, Make, Python 3.12 or newer, OpenSSH (ssh and scp) and Raspberry Pi Imager.
In your terminal, run the commands below.
Each prints a version or a path. `python3 --version` shows Python 3.12 or newer.
In the same terminal environment, list the files in `~/.ssh`. Look for a key pair, such as `id_ed25519` and `id_ed25519.pub`.
If you find a key pair, use it. Do not create another.
If you have no key, run the command below. Follow its prompts.
If `ssh-keygen` asks to overwrite an existing key, answer no. Never overwrite a key.
For the default key name, display `id_ed25519.pub` with the command below. Keep the whole public-key line for Imager.
If your key has another name, display its `.pub` file instead. Make SSH use that key for this Pi, through your SSH agent or an IdentityFile rule.
The key file without `.pub` is private. Never paste or share it.
steps.check: Each tool reports its version or path. Your public-key line is ready for Imager.
steps.note: You add this key in Imager in {step:imager-write}.

steps.title: Choose the Pi, system and card
actions: On your computer, open Raspberry Pi Imager.
Choose Raspberry Pi 3. This entry covers the Raspberry Pi 3 Model A+ board (E09).
Choose Raspberry Pi OS (other). Choose Raspberry Pi OS Lite (64-bit) in that list.
Check that its description names Trixie. The installer requires 64-bit Trixie with Python 3.13.
Insert the microSD card (E13) into your computer’s microSD reader (T10).
In Imager, select that card. Check its name and capacity.
If you cannot identify the card with confidence, stop. Do not write to that drive.
steps.check: Imager has Raspberry Pi 3, Raspberry Pi OS Lite (64-bit) and your microSD card selected.

steps.title: Set the Pi name, account and Wi-Fi
actions: Enter a unique hostname, for example `blooglyblob`. Use only letters, numbers and hyphens.
Write down your hostname. You need it for SSH and the repository settings.
On the Localisation screen, choose your country’s capital city, your time zone and your keyboard layout.
Continue to the User screen.
Choose a username and password for the Pi. This guide uses `builder` as its example username.
Write down your username. You need it for SSH and the repository settings.
Keep the password private. You need it at sudo prompts. Do not put it in the repository settings.
Enter your Wi-Fi network name and password.
Use a network where the Pi and your computer can reach each other. The Pi also needs internet access.

steps.title: Enable SSH and write the card
actions: Turn on Enable SSH. Select public-key authentication. Paste your public-key line, or select its `.pub` file.
If Imager suggests a key automatically, use it only if it is the key from your command environment.
If you use Windows, paste the key that `cat` shows in WSL, or select its `.pub` file in WSL. Windows and WSL keep separate keys. Keep using WSL for later commands.
Select NEXT.
If NEXT stays greyed out, check that the Public key box holds your whole public-key line.
On the Raspberry Pi Connect screen, leave Raspberry Pi Connect off. This build uses SSH.
On the Write image screen, check the device, operating system and storage.
Check that the summary lists five customisations: hostname, localisation, user account, Wi-Fi and SSH.
Select WRITE. Leave the card in the reader until writing and verification finish.
Imager shows “Write complete!” and ejects the card.
If your computer still shows the card, eject it.
Remove the microSD card from the reader.
steps.check: The card is written and verified. You have your hostname, username and SSH key ready.
steps.note: You displayed your public key in {step:computer-ssh-key}.

steps.title: Boot and connect to the Pi
actions: With power disconnected, insert the written microSD card into the Pi. Rest the bare board on a clean, nonconductive surface.
Plug the separate 5 V, 2.5 A micro-USB bench supply (T13) into the Pi’s micro-USB power port. Do not use the USB-A socket. It is for audio.
Allow a few minutes for the first boot and Wi-Fi connection.
In the terminal environment whose key you gave Imager, run the command below. Replace `builder` and `blooglyblob` with your username and hostname.
If ssh reports “Could not resolve hostname”, find the Pi’s IP address in your router’s device list. Use the IP address in place of the `.local` name.
On the first connection, ssh asks whether to trust the Pi’s host key. Accept it only if you are sure you are contacting that Pi.
If ssh reports “REMOTE HOST IDENTIFICATION HAS CHANGED”, stop. Correct `known_hosts` only after you confirm a reimaged card or a changed address.
A shell prompt with the Pi’s username and hostname, like the example below, means you are connected.
If access is denied, check the Imager username. Check that Imager has the public key from this terminal. Do not guess a different account.
Type `exit` to leave the Pi shell. Leave the Pi powered for the next step.
steps.check: You connected to the Pi with your SSH key and returned to your computer’s terminal. The Pi stays powered.

steps.title: Get the code and add your settings
actions: On your computer, run the commands below. They clone the repository and enter its folder.
If you already have this checkout, enter that folder instead. Do not clone another copy inside it.
Run every later Make command from this repository folder.
Run the commands below. Each copies an example only if its destination does not exist.
If you run them again, they keep your existing settings. Never replace your settings with a fresh example.
Open `.env` in a text editor. Set `PI_HOST` to your hostname plus `.local`, or to the IP address that worked for SSH.
Set `PI_USER` to your username. Keep `BLOOGLYBLOB_ENV_FILE=config/app.env`.
The example below matches `blooglyblob` and `builder`. These are lines in the file, not terminal commands. Do not add your Pi password or Wi-Fi password.
Create an API key in your own OpenAI account. Enable API billing for that account.
API usage is billed separately from a ChatGPT subscription. Your account needs access to the models listed in `config/app.env.example`.
Application startup can make a billable greeting request. Conversations also use paid API services.
Open `config/app.env` in your editor. Put your key after `OPENAI_API_KEY=`. Keep the other example settings.
Keep this file private. Git ignores it. Do not commit it, share it or show it in screenshots.
steps.check: Your computer has the repository, a `.env` file with your Pi target and a private `config/app.env` with your API key.

panels.title: Add the key to your settings

steps.title: Find and set the audio device
actions: Plug the male end of the USB-A extension cable (E23) into the Pi’s USB-A socket.
Plug the USB audio module (E14) into the extension’s female socket. Keep the module in its case on the bench.
On your computer, in the repository folder, run the command below. It opens SSH with the target in `.env`.
If the target is wrong or unreachable, correct `PI_HOST` and `PI_USER` in `.env`. Run the command again.
On the Pi, list the sound cards with the command below.
Note the USB name after “USB-Audio - ” and the card ID in brackets. The example shows the name USB PnP Audio Device and the ID `Device`.
If no USB audio card appears, check the module and extension connections. List the cards again.
In each command below, use your card ID for `Device`, not the card number. That number can change after a reboot. Run the three commands in order to read, set and save the Speaker level.
Both channels report `[-40.00dB]`, a low starting level.
If the Speaker control or its dB scale is missing, stop. Inspect the controls with `alsamixer -c Device` before you continue.
You adjust the level gradually in the later speaker check. After a reboot, recheck it with `amixer -c Device sget Speaker`.
Type `exit` to return to your computer.
On your computer, open `config/app.env`. Set `AUDIO_INPUT_DEVICE` and `AUDIO_OUTPUT_DEVICE` to the USB name you noted. If a line starts with `#`, remove the `#`.
Use the same name for both. The module provides the microphone and the speaker. A missing or ambiguous name stops startup. The application never picks another device.
Set `MIC_GAIN=1` to add no software gain to the microphone. It does not change speaker volume. Tune it only after a voice test.
steps.check: Both USB playback channels are saved at −40 dB. Your `config/app.env` names your USB audio device for input and output, with `MIC_GAIN=1`.

steps.title: Install the software
actions: On your computer, in the repository folder, run the command below.
The output must name your Pi 3, aarch64 or arm64, Python 3.13 and trixie.
If it rejects the model or OS, correct the choices in {step:imager-choose}. If SSH fails, fix the connection in {step:pi-connect}. Do not continue past a failed check.
Keep servo and lighting circuits disconnected. Only the USB audio module connects to the Pi now.
Run the command below. It installs the dependencies and starts the application. The application also starts at every boot.
If `sudo` asks for a password, enter the Pi account password. It is not saved in `.env`.
If it ends with “Installation complete”, continue to {step:service-check}.
If it stops with “Onboard audio is loaded”, reboot the Pi in the next panel. This is expected on the first run.
If it reports any other failure, fix the reported cause. Run `make pi-provision` again.
From your computer, open the Pi shell. Reboot the Pi. SSH disconnects during the reboot. The reboot frees the timer the lighting driver needs.
Wait for the Pi to rejoin Wi-Fi. Run `make pi-provision` again from your computer.
Provisioning keeps your existing settings on the Pi. First installation needs no extra `pi-update` step.
steps.check: Provisioning ends with “Installation complete; the application reached local readiness.”

steps.title: Check the service and shut down
actions: On your computer, in the repository folder, run the command below.
The output shows `active (running)`.
If it shows stopped or failed, read the log in the next panel. Do not mark setup complete.
Run the command below. It follows the application log.
If the log reports a missing key or audio device, correct the installed settings in panel 3. Editing `config/app.env` on your computer does not change the file on the Pi.
Press Ctrl+C to stop following the log.
If the service runs without configuration errors, skip this panel.
For a configuration error, open the Pi shell. Edit `/etc/blooglyblob/app.env` with `sudoedit`. Correct the key or device name. Save and close the editor. Type `exit`.
Back on your computer, restart the service. Check its status again.
From your computer, open the Pi shell. Shut the Pi down with the second command. The SSH session disconnects.
Wait for the Pi’s green activity light to stop flashing. Unplug the bench supply (T13) from the Pi.
Unplug the USB extension (E23) from the Pi. Unplug the audio module (E14) from the extension.
steps.check: The application runs with its USB audio device. The Pi is shut down, unplugged and ready to mount.

steps.title: Mount the Pi and level shifters
actions: Label the two level shifters (E15) as level shifter (S1) and level shifter (S2).
On the back of each board, find the copper jumper labeled Neo, beside the top mounting hole. Cutting it disables only the onboard test LED.
Cut only the narrow bridge inside its white outline. With the meter in continuity mode, check that each cut is open. Both signal channels on each board stay active.
Place the base (FB01) upside down, with its open bottom facing up.
Find the Pi mounts at the rear and the two level shifter positions in front of them.
Mark S1 nearer the Pi and S2 nearer the audio cradle.
Mark GPIO pin 1 beside the Pi header. Pin 1 is at the microSD end, farthest from the full-size USB port. Its underside pad is square.
Place the Pi (E09) with its components toward the open bottom. Point its full-size USB port toward the audio cradle and its microSD end toward the rear wall.
Check that the USB and power plugs fit without pressing on nearby parts. Fit four M2×12 screws. Tighten them only until secure, without bowing the board.
Fit S1 in the position nearer the Pi and S2 in the position nearer the audio cradle. Face their components and screw heads toward the open bottom.
Fasten each board with two M2×10 screws into the seated nuts. Use no washers. Keep the terminal entries and both frame-screw paths clear.
Both level shifters sit flat on their posts.
steps.check: All three boards sit flat and their nuts stay bonded. Screw tips clear components. The sockets stay reachable.
steps.note: You glued the eight board nuts in {step:board-cover-nuts}.

steps.title: Mount and label the four WAGOs
actions: Clean and dry the backs of the four WAGOs (E06) and their pads in the base. Follow the instructions for the double-sided mounting tape (C16).
Cut a piece of tape to fit the flat back of each WAGO. Keep it clear of the levers and wire entries.
Place each WAGO with its wire entries toward the robot’s front and its levers toward the open bottom.
Test-fit all four WAGOs with the tape thickness included. Each lever must open fully without touching the cover or nearby parts.
Remove the liners. Press each WAGO onto its pad. Let the tape bond for its stated time before wiring.
Beside the pads, label the four WAGOs from rear to front.
Rear to front: input WAGO (W1), ground WAGO (W3), servo power WAGO (W2), servo ground WAGO (W4). W1 and W2 carry +5 V. W3 and W4 carry GND.
Open and close each lever gently to check the bond.
Number each WAGO’s ports from the robot-right end. In this open-bottom view, port 1 is on the picture’s right.
All five ports in one WAGO are joined.
Use this numbering for all four WAGOs. In this guide, W1/3 means WAGO W1, port 3.
steps.check: All four WAGOs stay bonded while their levers open. The labels and wire entries are visible.

steps.title: Mount the audio cradle
actions: Set the loose audio cradle (FB24) on the bench, open side up. Slide an M2 nut sideways into each end pocket. Work from the middle outward. Keep the nut flats parallel to the slot walls.
Each nut sits at the outer end of its pocket.
Keep the cradle open side up and level from now on, or the nuts can slide out.
With the base upside down, lower the cradle into it, open side up and level. Place it directly behind the front microphone grille, clear of the grille screw tips.
Put three M3×6 screws through the cradle into the glued nuts. Use no washers. Fit the middle screw now. The audio module will cover it. Start all three screws by hand. Tighten them gently.
The cradle sits flat in the base, with both lid nuts still in their pockets.
steps.check: The empty cradle is screwed to the base at all three mounting holes. Both M2 lid nuts are seated.
steps.note: You glued the cradle nuts in {step:cradle-jack-nuts}. The lid screws go into the lid nuts in {step:audio-module}.

steps.title: Fit the USB audio module
actions: Check that the socket end of the USB-A extension cable (E23) passes through the cradle end opening without force.
If it does not, leave the module out. The cable route or connector fit needs resolving first.
Clean the back of the USB audio module (E14) case and the inside rear wall of the cradle. Follow the instructions for the double-sided mounting tape (C16).
Apply a patch of the tape under 1 mm thick to the back of the case, opposite the microphones. Keep it inside the flat face. Do not tape the lid.
Remove the outer tape liner.
With the base still upside down and level, lower the module into the cradle. Keep both cables disconnected. Face its microphones toward the front grille.
Keep the tape clear of the wall until the case is seated.
Press the case rearward so the tape bonds to the inside rear wall. Use the pressure and bonding time in the tape instructions.
The case stays against the rear wall when you let go.
Through the end openings, connect the USB-A extension cable, 200 mm or shorter.
Connect the four-wire speaker cable. Connect each labeled speaker to its matching output. The speaker outputs do not connect to power ground.
Leave the Pi end of the extension cable disconnected until {step:button-audio-wiring}.
Line the audio cradle lid (FB32) with 1 mm foam (C10). Keep its openings clear.
Fit the lid with two M2×8 screws into the cradle nuts. Use no washers. Tighten gently, without squeezing the case or trapping cables.
If a lid screw does not catch, remove the lid. Push its nut back to the outer end of its pocket.
steps.check: The case is taped to the inside rear wall and the lid is fitted. The microphones and cable connections are unobstructed.

steps.title: Prepare the button leads
actions: On the back of the button (E17), find the LED and switch terminals. Label each one.
The closer upper pair is LED − and LED +. The wider lower pair is the switch.
With the meter in continuity mode, check that the lower switch pair closes only while you press the button.
On the bench, slide heat-shrink onto four GPIO jumper leads (E24).
Solder three quick-connect wires (E19) to three of the GPIO leads. Keep the female sockets at the Pi ends.
Slide heat-shrink onto the fourth quick-connect wire. Solder the button LED resistor (R1), 1 kΩ, between that wire and the fourth GPIO lead. This is the LED + lead.
Insulate every splice and both resistor joints.
No bare metal shows at any joint.
Label each Pi end with its Pi pin. Switch leads: pins 11 and 14. LED + lead through R1: pin 4. LED − lead: pin 20. Leave the four Pi ends disconnected until {step:button-audio-wiring}.

steps.title: Fit the front button
actions: On the bench, put the button (E17) through the button insert (FB20) from the outside.
Tighten the button’s supplied retaining nut against the back of the insert.
Push the prepared quick-connects onto their matching terminals. Cover exposed contact metal with separate insulating sleeves.
Keep the connectors removable. Keep the insulated joints clear of the retaining nut.
Keep the base (FB01) upside down, with its open bottom facing up. Keep it level until both screws are in. Do not glue these nuts.
Through the open bottom, drop an M3 nut into the pocket beside the button opening, away from the foot post. Match its flats to the pocket.
Beside the foot post, slide a second M3 nut sideways into its pocket from the button opening. Match its flats to the pocket.
Slide the base over the front edge of the bench until you can reach the button opening from below. Keep most of the base on the bench.
From below, feed the leads and the button body up through the opening. Leave enough slack to remove the insert.
Hold the insert flush in its opening, clear of the screw bosses and foot post.
With your other hand, fit an M3×8 screw up through the insert into a nut. Use no washer. Turn it by hand until it catches.
If a screw does not catch, check that its nut is still in its pocket.
Fit the second M3×8 screw the same way. Tighten both screws gently. Do not use the screws to pull the insert into place. Slide the base back onto the bench.
steps.check: All soldered joints are insulated and the switch closes only when pressed. The button insert sits flush without pinching its leads. The four labeled Pi ends stay disconnected.

steps.title: Prepare and fit the power jack
actions: On the bench, away from printed parts, find the center-pin and sleeve lugs of the power jack (J1). Use the meter in continuity mode.
The center pin is +5 V. The sleeve is the return. The third, switched lug stays unused.
Solder an 18 AWG lead to each of those two lugs. Label each lead with its function. The return lead may need 150–160 mm.
Insulate each joint and the unused switched lug separately.
With the meter in continuity mode, check each lead again. Check that there is no short between center and sleeve.
Let the joints cool before mounting. Leave the leads long for final routing.
Push J1 through the power jack plate (FB21) from the back. Its leads stay behind the plate. Fit the supplied washer and nut on the outside.
Check full thread engagement and clearance around the insulated lugs.
Place the base (FB01) upside down. Feed the leads and the jack body into the base through the power jack opening.
Seat the plate flush against the outside of the base. The jack body holds it loosely in its opening.
Through the open bottom, place an M3 nut in the pocket nearer the open bottom. Match its flats to the pocket. Hold it there with a fingertip. Do not glue it.
With your other hand, put an M3×12 screw through the plate into that nut. Use no washer. Turn it by hand until it catches.
Repeat for the other pocket. Reach past the jack body to hold its nut. Tighten both screws evenly. Leave enough lead slack to remove the plate.
The plate sits flat against the base.
steps.check: The jack cannot rotate. The center and sleeve leads are labeled and insulated. The plate comes off without pulling a joint.

steps.title: Connect the power jack, Pi power lead and ground
actions: Test-route the J1 center lead to the input WAGO (W1/1). Test-route the sleeve lead to the ground WAGO (W3/1). Cut each lead where it reaches.
Strip 11 mm from each lead. Do not tin it. Open the lever at W1/1. Push the bare center lead fully in. Close the lever.
Insert the sleeve lead into W3/1 the same way. Each WAGO 221-415 port takes one wire. Pull gently on each wire. It must stay in the port.
Cut the USB-C end off the Pi power lead (E22). Keep the micro-B plug. Leave the cable long for now. Label the lead PI POWER.
Strip back the outer jacket. With the meter in continuity mode, find the wire from plug pin 1. It is +5 V. The wire from pin 5 is GND.
Label the +5 V and GND wires. Insulate each of the other wires separately with heat-shrink.
Plug the micro-B plug into the Pi’s power socket. Test-route the +5 V wire to W1/2. Test-route the GND wire to W3/2. Use gentle bends through the gaps in the WAGO row.
The finished 24 AWG lead, plug included, must be 150 mm or shorter. Do not add an extension or a service loop. Check that both wires reach before you cut them.
Cut both wires where they reach. Insert the +5 V wire into W1/2. Insert the GND wire into W3/2.
Cut one 18 AWG wire (C05) long enough to reach from W3/3 to the servo ground WAGO (W4/1). Strip 11 mm at each end.
Insert one end into W3/3. Insert the other end into W4/1.
Leave W1/5 and W4/5 empty.
steps.check: The power jack center reaches W1. Its sleeve reaches W3 and W4. The Pi power lead’s polarity is correct, and it is 150 mm or shorter, plug included.

steps.title: Wire the servo fuse and capacitor
actions: The servo fuse (F1) sits between the input WAGO (W1) and the servo power WAGO (W2). All three servos draw their power through F1.
Label one fuse holder (E07) F1. Its fuse is T3.15 A. Keep the fuse out of the holder while you wire.
Lay the holder toward the front of the base, as shown. Keep its opening where you can reach it.
Test-route the holder’s loop from W1/3 to W2/1. Mark the loop where both ends reach without tension. Cut the loop once at the mark.
If the output end is short, solder on an 18 AWG extension at the bench. Insulate the joint.
If the input end is short, do not extend it. Change the layout instead.
Strip 11 mm from each end of the F1 loop. Insert the input end into W1/3. Insert the output end into W2/1.
Place the holder where you can open it. Keep W2/2 to W2/4 free for the three servos.
F1 is the only path from W1 to W2.
Label one 1000 µF, 10 V capacitor (E08) C1. The stripe on its body marks the negative leg. On the bench, solder an 18 AWG wire to each leg. Mark the negative wire.
Cover each leg and its joint with its own heat-shrink. Lay C1 beside the WAGO row. Cut each wire to reach its port.
Insert the positive wire into W2/5. Insert the negative wire into W3/4. Bend the wires gently at the rubber-seal end. Keep the vent end uncovered.
steps.check: F1 is the only path from W1 to W2. C1 polarity is correct. Its two insulated wires are separate.

steps.title: Wire the light fuse and capacitor
actions: The light fuse (F2) carries power from the input WAGO (W1) to the body light connector. Label the second fuse holder (E07) F2. Its fuse is T1 A. Keep it out while you wire.
Lay the holder toward the rear of the base. Test-route its loop from W1/4 to the harness opening. Mark the loop where both ends reach without tension. Cut the loop once at the mark.
If the output end is short, solder on an 18 AWG extension at the bench. Insulate the joint. Do not extend the input end.
Choose one three-pin JST-SM pair (E10) for the body light connector. Label both halves BODY LIGHT. Label each wire +5 V, GND or DATA.
Plug the two halves together. With the meter in continuity mode, check that each wire reaches the same-labeled wire on the other half.
Unplug the halves. The base half stays in the base. Keep the body half for {step:body-light-input}.
Label the second 1000 µF, 10 V capacitor (E08) C2. It stays on the base side of the connector. On the bench, slide heat-shrink onto the wires before you solder.
Solder the F2 output end, the base-half +5 V wire and the C2 positive leg in one joint. Solder the C2 striped negative leg to the base-half GND wire.
Cover each joint and each C2 leg with its own heat-shrink. Keep the 22 AWG power wires and their branches apart. No bare metal may touch another conductor.
Strip 11 mm from the F2 input end. Insert it into W1/4.
Strip 11 mm from the base-half GND wire. Insert it into the ground WAGO (W3/5). It is the only wire in W3/5.
Label the base-half DATA wire for terminal D5 of the level shifter (S1). You connect it in the next step. Leave the body light connector unplugged.
steps.check: F2 feeds the base-half +5 V wire. C2 polarity is correct. Each branch joint is insulated on its own.

steps.title: Connect the level shifters
actions: Take the remaining eight GPIO jumper leads (E24). They connect the Pi to the two level shifters (S1, S2).
Keep the 2.54 mm female socket on one end of each lead. That end goes on the Pi.
Cut off any connector at the other end. Strip only enough for the bare wire to fit fully inside a screw terminal.
Find pin 1, marked at the microSD end of the header. Connect pin 1 to S1 V. Connect pin 6 to S1 G. Connect pin 12 to S1 DAT. Connect pin 32 to S1 CLK.
For each lead, hold the socket by its plastic body. Push it straight down onto its Pi pin. Push the bare end fully into its S1 terminal. Tighten the terminal screw.
Connect the base-half DATA wire to S1 D5. Label S1 C5 LEFT. Leave S1 !D5 and the output G terminal empty.
Connect pin 17 to S2 V. Connect pin 9 to S2 G. Connect pin 33 to S2 DAT. Connect pin 36 to S2 CLK. Use the same method as for S1.
Label S2 D5 RIGHT. Label S2 C5 HEAD. Leave S2 !D5 and the output G terminal empty.
Each socket sits on one pin. No bare strands show outside any terminal.
steps.check: Eight Pi pins connect to S1 and S2 as in the diagrams. The base-half DATA wire is in S1 D5. The three servo output terminals are labeled.
steps.note: You prepared the four button leads in {step:button-leads}. You cut the Neo jumpers in {step:pi-shifters}.

steps.title: Connect the button and USB audio
actions: Find the two switch leads from the lower button terminals. They are labeled 11 and 14.
Push the switch lead labeled 11 onto Pi pin 11 (GPIO17). Push the switch lead labeled 14 onto pin 14 (GND).
Push the LED + lead, with the button LED resistor (R1) in it, onto pin 4 (+5 V). Push the LED − lead onto pin 20 (GND).
Keep this upper LED pair separate from the lower switch pair. The Pi header powers the button light.
Both LED contacts and every joint are insulated.
Plug the USB extension (E23) into the Pi’s full-size USB socket. Its other end is already in the audio module.
Check that both speaker plugs are seated in the module.
Route the USB cable around the audio cradle in one relaxed bend. Keep the bend on the open-bottom side of the cradle. Do not pull sideways on either socket.
steps.check: All twelve Pi header connections match their physical pin numbers. The switch, button light and speaker circuits are separate. The USB cable bends without pulling on either socket.

steps.title: Secure the fuses, capacitors and wires
actions: Lay the servo fuse (F1) toward the front. Lay the light fuse (F2) toward the rear. Lay the servo capacitor (C1) and light capacitor (C2) beside the WAGO row.
Keep each fuse holder’s opening reachable. Keep each capacitor’s vent end uncovered.
Choose where your wiring needs support. Place 1 × 1-inch adhesive tie squares (C17) there, on flat inside faces, with their liners still on.
Check that each square makes full contact. Its tie lock and the wiring must stay at least 4 mm from the bottom cover (FB02).
Prepare each surface as the square’s instructions say. Peel the liner. Press the square down. Let it bond for the time in its instructions before loading it.
Tie each fuse holder and capacitor body to a tie square with a cable tie (C07). Keep ties off capacitor ends and fuse openings.
Tighten each tie only enough to stop sliding. Trim the tails.
Each body is held by its tie, not by its wires.
Route every wire around both frame-screw positions. Keep the harness opening clear. The three servo cables and the body half of the body light connector pass through it later.
Where wires run together, such as the eight GPIO leads, tie them to the nearest square. Tie the F2 output end so that cutting one tie frees it. Trim the tails.
Keep the SD card, WAGO levers, fuse caps, plugs and vents reachable. Leave each tie lock where you can cut it.
steps.check: The fuse holders, capacitors and tied wires are held by ties, not by their terminals. Each tie square holds.

steps.title: Check the unpowered base
actions: Keep the servo fuse (F1) and light fuse (F2) out of their holders. With the meter in continuity mode, check that the power jack (J1) center reaches the input WAGO (W1).
Check that the J1 sleeve reaches the ground WAGO (W3). Check that W3 reaches the servo ground WAGO (W4).
Unplug the Pi power lead from the Pi. Check that plug pin 1 reaches W1 and pin 5 reaches W3. Plug the lead back in.
Check that W1 does not reach the servo power WAGO (W2). A connection here means a wire bypasses F1.
Check W1 against W3, and W2 against W4, for a +5 V-to-ground short. The meter may beep briefly while a capacitor charges. It must not beep steadily.
If you find a bypass or a steady beep, find and fix the fault before you go on.
Check each fuse on its own for continuity. F1 is T3.15 A. F2 is T1 A.
Fit F1. Check that W1 now reaches W2 through it. Remove F1 again.
Fit F2 for the light test. It stays fitted. Check W1 against W3 again in continuity mode. It must not beep steadily. If it does, remove F2. Fix the short before you go on.
Compare the level shifter (S1, S2) and button wiring with their diagrams. Check that every WAGO lever is closed and every terminal is tight.
Check the polarity of the servo capacitor (C1) and light capacitor (C2). Check that every joint is insulated. Check that neither speaker’s negative wire connects to ground.
Remove wire offcuts and debris.
steps.check: The unpowered checks pass. F1 is out of its holder and F2 (T1 A) is fitted.

panels.caption: The three branches from W1, with both fuses shown in place.

panels.title: Check for a fuse bypass or a short

safety.text: The two fuses look alike. A T3.15 A fuse in the F2 holder would let a light fault overheat the thin wires. Read each fuse’s marking before you fit it.

steps.title: Prepare the body light input
actions: On the body light strand (E05), find the wire with a copper coil or dots. It is +5 V. The middle wire is normally DATA. The other wire is GND.
Label the three wires at each end. If the markings are missing or disagree, ask the vendor before you go on.
Hold one end’s connector upward with a pebble’s resin bump facing you. If the marked +5 V wire is on the left, that end is the likely input. The light test in {step:body-light-test} confirms it.
On the bench, label the strand’s factory leads at the likely input. Cut off only that end’s connector, keeping the wire length. Do not cut the strand. Keep all 100 pebbles together.
Take the body half of the body light connector (E10) from {step:light-fuse-capacitor}. Leave its wires long. You test-route them in {step:body-light-strand}.
Solder the data resistor (R2), 330 Ω, between the body half’s DATA wire and the strand’s DATA wire. Keep R2 near the first pebble. Insulate both joints.
Cut two 22 AWG wires (C06) for the head power pair, one +5 V and one GND. Leave them long.
Solder three +5 V wires in one joint: the body half’s, the strand’s and the pair’s. Join the three GND wires the same way.
Insulate both joints separately. Cap each free end of the head power pair separately.
steps.check: The input harness (body half, R2 and head power pair) is soldered to the likely input. Every joint is insulated and both head power pair ends are capped.

panels.title: Identify the strand wires and the likely input
Cut the connector off the likely input
Solder the data resistor into the DATA wire
Solder the power joints with the head power pair

steps.title: Test the body light input
actions: Check the base. The servo fuse (F1) is out and the light fuse (F2), T1 A, is fitted. No servo is connected. Both head power pair ends are capped.
With the meter in continuity mode, check the body half’s +5 V and GND contacts. Each must reach its matching wire at the strand’s far end. Check that +5 V does not reach GND.
Plug the body half into the base half.
Use the Mean Well GST40A05-P1J supply, 5 V, 5 A. Plug it into the wall with the mains cord (E21). Keep its barrel plug away from the base.
Set the meter to DC volts. Put the red probe in the plug’s center. Touch the black probe to its outer sleeve.
The meter must read 5.0–5.25 V with no minus sign. If it does not, do not use this supply. Either way, unplug the supply from the wall.
Push the barrel plug fully into the power jack (J1). Plug the supply into the wall. Let the Pi boot.
If you notice smoke, an unusual smell or overheating, unplug the supply at once.
From your computer, run the two commands below. The first stops the application. The second lights the first 16 pebbles at brightness 128.
The first 16 pebbles light one at a time from the connected end. Color patterns follow. The test clears all 16 when it ends.
The output names eye and mouth lights, but on this strand they are all pebbles. If any of the other 84 pebbles light, unplug the supply and find the fault.
Open the Pi shell. Shut the Pi down with the second command.
Wait for the Pi’s green activity light to stop flashing. Unplug the supply from the wall. Unplug the barrel plug from J1.
Unplug the body half from the base half.
If the first 16 pebbles lit in order from the connected end, mark that end INPUT. Mark INPUT only after a passing light test.
If nothing lit, check the power, DATA and contacts first. If they are correct, move the input harness to the other end of the strand. Repeat this step.
After a move, insulate the three wires at the abandoned end separately. Keep the input harness attached. Do not cut the strand until an end passes.
steps.check: The connected end passed the light test and is marked INPUT. The input harness stays attached, with the data resistor (R2) and its capped head power pair. The supply is unplugged.
steps.note: You cut the strand to six lights in {step:body-light-strand}.

steps.title: Attach the frame uprights
actions: Rest the base (FB01) on its robot-left side on a folded towel. Turn its open bottom toward you. The top wall now faces away from you.
Inside the base, move any wire away from the screw holes in front of and behind the central opening. Keep the opening clear.
Slide an M3 nut into the slot near the foot of each frame upright (P02). When fitted, the slots face away from the other upright.
With one hand, hold a foam collar (P01) on the outside of the top wall. Line up its two tabs with the screw holes.
With the same hand, hold one upright on its tab, slots facing outward. With the other hand, put an M3×16 screw from inside through the top wall and collar into the upright.
Turn the screw by hand until it catches the nut. Fasten the other upright the same way. Tighten both screws evenly.
steps.check: Both uprights are firm and parallel. The collar sits flat and no wire is trapped.

steps.title: Prepare the three servo cables
actions: On each servo (E01), find the supply, ground and signal wires. Use the Kitronik 25105 datasheet linked from the servo’s part card.
Label the left arm servo cable LEFT at both ends. Label the right arm servo cable RIGHT and the head servo cable HEAD the same way.
Cut off the crocodile clips one wire at a time. Keep each label on the servo side of the cut. Keep the cut ends apart.
Keep the base on its side. With one hand, hold each servo near its place on the frame. With the other hand, test-route its cable through the central opening into the base.
LEFT reaches the servo power WAGO (W2/2), the servo ground WAGO (W4/2) and level shifter (S1) C5. RIGHT reaches W2/3, W4/3 and level shifter (S2) D5.
HEAD reaches W2/4, W4/4 and S2 C5. Mark each wire where it reaches with slack. Keep any joint clear of moving parts.
If a wire is short or thinner than 24 AWG, extend it at the bench. Solder on 22 AWG wire (C06). Cover the joint with heat-shrink (C12).
Strip 11 mm from each supply and ground wire for its WAGO port. Strip the signal wire so its bare end fits entirely inside its level shifter terminal.
steps.check: All three servo cables are labeled at both ends and reach their ports with slack. Every extension joint is insulated.

steps.title: Mount the shoulder servos
actions: On the bench, press an M2 nut into each hex pocket on the inner faces of the shoulder-servo bracket (P03). There are four pockets.
Each nut sits flat in its pocket.
Hold the bracket with its open long side toward you. This side faces the robot’s back.
Slide the LEFT servo in on your left, shaft pointing robot-left. Rest its ears on the supports. Keep its cable toward the middle of the bracket.
Fit the RIGHT servo on your right the same way, shaft pointing robot-right.
Put an M2×6 screw through each servo ear into its nut. Fit all four before the bracket goes on the frame.
Tighten each screw until its servo sits firm. Stop before the ears bow. Keep the horns off.
Stand the base on its feet. Lower the bracket between the uprights, open side toward the back. Line up its holes with the round holes in the uprights.
Push both rear M3×16 screws through the rear upright into the bracket, with no nuts. They hold the bracket while you work.
Start at the lower front hole. Hold an M3 nut in the front access well with fine pliers. Put an M3×16 screw through the upright into it. Repeat at the upper hole.
If a nut drops through a well, find it before you go on. The wells are open at the bottom. Do not leave a loose nut in the base.
Back out one rear screw until its tip leaves the rear access well. Hold a nut in the well with fine pliers. Turn the screw in until it catches.
Repeat for the other rear screw. Tighten all four screws evenly. Keep the uprights straight. A small gap around each servo body is normal.
steps.check: Neither servo rocks, all ears sit flat and the bracket is secure without bowed uprights.

steps.title: Mount the head servo and upper foam collar
actions: On the bench, press an M2 nut into each of the two hex pockets under the head-servo bracket (P04).
Slide the HEAD servo into the bracket’s open side, shaft up. Rest its ears on the supports. Keep its cable pointing down.
Put an M2×6 screw down through each ear into its nut. Fit both before the bracket goes on the frame.
Tighten until the servo cannot rock or slide.
Hold the bracket against the robot-left side of both uprights, near their tops, open side robot-left. From robot-left, push an M3×20 screw through the bracket and the side hole in each upright.
At the uprights’ robot-right faces, hold an M3 nut on one screw tip with a fingertip. Turn the screw until it catches. Repeat for the other screw. Tighten both screws.
Route the servo cable down the frame. Keep it clear of the shaft, where the head horn fits.
Slide an M3 nut into the slot near the top of each upright, from its outer face.
Place the second foam collar (P01) on the upright tops, tabs over the holes. Put an M3×10 screw down through each tab into its nut. Tighten both.
The head-bracket screw heads stay reachable from robot-left.
steps.check: The head-servo bracket is firm and the upper collar is level. The servo shaft points up, with a clear cable path.

steps.title: Prepare the three servo horns
actions: Keep each round servo horn (E02) with its center screw. Work with each horn off its servo.
On each horn, choose one opposite hole pair about 18 mm apart. Measure it on your horn. Support the disk. Drill both holes to 2.2 mm.
Remove burrs and drilling debris. Leave the central spline and center hole unchanged.
steps.check: Two M2 screws pass freely through each drilled pair. All three center splines are undamaged.
steps.note: The horns go on the servo shafts in {step:shelf-arms}, after {step:fit-position}.

steps.title: Build the head shelf on the bench
actions: Hold the head horn adapter (P14) flange up. Slide an M2 nut into each of the two side slots in its hub.
Hold a drilled horn (E02) in the recess under the adapter. Its flat disk goes against the adapter. Its long splined hub faces away, toward the servo.
Line up the drilled holes with the nuts. Put an M2×6 screw up through each hole into its nut. Tighten both. Keep the horn’s center screw aside.
Hold the head shelf (P08) off the bench, with its three M3 nut pockets facing down. Lower the adapter’s hub through the shelf’s center from above.
Rest the flange on the shelf. Line up its three holes with the shelf’s holes.
Drop an M3×8 screw down through the flange and shelf at each hole. The screw heads rest on the flange.
Keep the shelf level in one hand. With a fingertip of that hand, press an M3 nut up into the pocket under one screw.
With your other hand, turn that screw with a hex key until it catches the nut. Repeat for the other two screws.
Tighten all three screws. Keep the shelf’s open cable entry clear.
steps.check: The horn, adapter and shelf are secure. The screw heads sit on the flange, and the nuts sit in the pockets below. The cable entry and the horn’s center hole are clear.
steps.note: The shelf goes on the head servo in {step:shelf-arms}.

steps.title: Fit the eye windows and diffusers
actions: Print the eye film template at full size. Cut two windows from clear film (C01): 12.6 × 8.6 mm, with 4.2 mm corner radii. The template also has small fit alternatives.
Hold the robot-right eye housing (GS11) off the head. Bow the film gently into the groove behind the front lip. Let it flatten with its whole edge captured.
Fit the robot-left eye housing (GS12) the same way.
Cut two 14 × 10 mm patches of 4 mm white Plastazote LD45 eye foam (C02).
Place one patch in each housing, behind the window. Keep the mounting holes clear.
Lay each housing window-down so the foam stays in place.
steps.check: Both windows sit flat with their edges captured. The foam is not crushed.

safety.text: Thick film does not fit behind the 0.6 mm lip. Forcing it can crack the lip. Use a clear, flexible transparency sheet that bows in without force.

panels.caption: A foam patch going into the housing behind the film.

steps.title: Seat the eye housings
actions: Use standard M2 nuts, 4 mm across flats and 1.6 mm thick. Keep each housing off the head.
Slide one nut into each channel from the upper edge, flats parallel to the front. Push it until it sits beneath its screw-hole roof.
Do not push a nut through its round hole. Do not glue the nuts.
Seat the robot-right eye housing (GS11) in its socket on the head shell (GS20), from the face side. Seat the robot-left eye housing (GS12) the same way.
Their short tapered pegs align them. They do not snap in. Hold them in place with your fingers.
Turn the head face-down onto a folded towel. Keep it face-down until the eye cassettes are fastened. This keeps the loose nuts and foam in place.
steps.check: Both housings sit without force. Each has two seated nuts. The film and foam lie flat.

panels.title: Seat the housings on the head

steps.title: Fit the eye boards and straps
actions: Press two M2 nuts into the rectangular pockets on the flat side of each eye LED cassette (P06). This side faces the foam. The nuts sit above and below the light opening.
Turn the cassette over onto the bench, so the bench holds the nuts in. Seat an eye board (E03) on its supports, LED facing into the light opening.
Its IN and OUT sockets face away from the cassette. Fit two M2×6 screws, with no washers. Tighten them lightly.
Fit the other board the same way.
Put an M2 washer on each of two M2×10 screws. From inside the head, pass them through a cassette’s outer holes and the head wall into the housing nuts.
Tighten until the nuts seat under their roofs. Do not force a screw that bottoms out. Fasten the other cassette the same way.
Fit both eyes now: the mouth blocks straight access to these screws later. All four eye sockets stay reachable.
Test-fit the robot-left head strap (GS01), robot-right head strap (GS02) and rear head strap (GS03). Check that they clear the eye housing joints.
Glue only the locating pegs with two-part epoxy (C09). Keep glue off the housing joints, the center seam and the two rear seams. Do not clamp the rear seams shut.
Let the epoxy cure fully, for the time on its label.
steps.check: Each eye removes and refits independently. Only the strap locating pegs are glued. The housings sit flat and their retaining roofs are intact.

steps.title: Wire the head harness
actions: Take the other three-pin JST-SM pair (E10) for the head light connector. Label both halves HEAD LIGHT. Label each wire +5 V, GND or DATA.
Plug the halves together. With the meter in continuity mode, check that each wire reaches the same-labeled wire on the other half. Match by function, not by connector sex.
Unplug the halves. The head half stays with the head. Keep the body half for {step:body-light-strand}.
Choose either eye as the first eye. Note its side. The first eye is light 6, the second eye light 7 and the mouth lights 8 to 15.
Place the mouth stick (E04) loosely at the mouth inside the head. Test-route three 22 AWG leads (C06) from it toward the first eye. Leave slack to fit and remove the mouth.
Take the stick out of the head. On the bench, solder the +5 V, GND and DIN leads to their pads. Leave DOUT unused. Insulate each joint. Label each lead.
Keep every eye plug unplugged until all joints are insulated and cool. Cut the header pins off both JST-SH eye leads (E11). Keep their plugs.
Join the head half’s +5 V wire, the first eye lead’s red wire and the mouth +5 V lead. Solder them in one joint at the bench.
Join the three GND wires the same way, with the eye lead’s black wire. Insulate each joint separately.
Solder the head half’s DATA wire to the first eye lead’s DATA wire. Insulate the joint.
Solder the second eye lead’s DATA wire to the mouth DIN lead. Insulate the joint. Insulate its unused red and black wires separately.
With the meter in continuity mode, touch the head half’s +5 V and GND contacts. The meter must not beep steadily. Check DATA against +5 V and against GND the same way.
If the meter beeps steadily, find and fix the short before you plug in the eyes.
Plug the first eye lead into the first eye’s IN socket. Press the plug housing, not its wires.
Connect the 100 mm eye cable (E12) from the first eye’s OUT to the second eye’s IN. Plug the second eye lead into the second eye’s OUT.
Tie the eye wires at the eye LED cassettes (P06), with slack and joints clear of bends. Support the wired mouth beside the head until {step:mouth}. Do not let it hang from its wires.
steps.check: Mouth power bypasses the eye cable. All joints are insulated and the eye plugs are seated. The wired mouth stays loose, ready for the next step.

steps.title: Assemble the mouth
actions: Support the wired mouth stick (E04) on the bench. Hold it against the mouth LED cassette (P30), LEDs facing away from the cassette.
Put two M2×8 screws through the stick and the cassette’s inner holes, from the LED side. Fit an M2 nut on each. Use no washers.
Keep the LED faces clear. The black cassette is not electrical insulation, so keep every joint covered.
Keep the head face-down on the towel. Slide an M2 nut into the slot in each mouth boss. Each slot opens toward the middle of the mouth.
Cut a strip of 4 mm white mouth foam (C03), 7.4 mm high and slightly long. Curve it into the mouth pocket. Trim its ends until it lies flat without bunching or stretching.
Place the mouth light separator (P31) behind the foam, curved face against it. Its eight channels face the LEDs. Place the cassette behind it.
From the rear, put an M2×8 screw through each outer cassette hole into a head nut. Use no washers. Tighten both. Tie the wires at the cassette without pulling a joint.
steps.check: All eight LEDs align behind the smile, with the end LEDs in their channels. The gaps of about 0.7 mm to the LED faces and 2.3 mm to the board stay empty. The foam lies flat. The cassette can come out through the open rim.

panels.caption: The separator and cassette, with the two outer clamp screws.

steps.title: Fit the antenna
actions: Start the large thread of the antenna coil (A04) straight into the socket on top of the head. Hand-tighten it gently until it seats.
Support the coil tip. Screw the antenna ball (A05) onto it straight, by hand. Do not glue the threads. Do not use the ball as a handle.
If either thread binds, stop. Clean support from the thread and try again.
steps.check: The antenna base sits flush. The ball unscrews without twisting the coil.
steps.note: You can fit the antenna later, in {step:secure-wiring}, to protect it while you assemble.

panels.title: Screw on the coil and ball
panels.caption: The coil and ball above the head’s threaded socket.

steps.title: Prepare the head light cable and fasteners
actions: Hold the head and the shelf separately. Test-fit an M2 nut in each of the three pockets on top of the head shelf (P08). Each nut stands on edge.
Test-fit an M2×8 button-head screw in each of the head shell (GS20) recesses, on its two sides and back. Use no washers or plugs.
The recesses suit Ø3.5 × 1.3 mm heads. The pockets suit nuts 4 mm across flats and 1.6 mm thick. Set them aside for {step:head-shoulder-covers}.
Hold the head on the shelf. Lay the head harness wires into the shelf’s open side entry, from the side. Keep them clear of the horn screws.
Leave the head half below the shelf. Do not force the plug through a closed hole. This path is separate from the head servo cable.
Leave a relaxed loop below the shelf. The head turns with the servo while the body stays still.
Lift the head a little off the shelf. Check that you can reach and release the head light connector latch. Keep the wires clear of the horn and screw tips.
Take the head off the shelf. Keep both off the servo until after {step:fit-position}.
steps.check: The fasteners fit freely. The head harness can turn and unplug without pulling on an LED board.

panels.title: Test-fit the head screws and nuts
panels.caption: The head shelf from above, with the three nut pockets.

panels.title: Lay the harness into the shelf entry
panels.caption: The shelf’s side entry, with the harness laid in from the side.

panels.title: Leave slack to turn and lift the head
panels.caption: An example loop below the shelf.

steps.title: Prepare the body light strand
actions: Count six pebbles from the end marked INPUT. Cut the wire midway between the sixth and seventh pebbles.
On the rest of the strand, mark the new cut end INPUT. Store it as spare lights.
Label the six pebbles light 0 to light 5, starting at INPUT.
Test-route the body half of the body light connector down the frame. Pass it through the central opening to the base half in the base.
Test-route the head power pair up the frame, through the upper foam collar (P01). Mark the pair where it reaches with slack to lift the head and unplug the head light connector.
If either cable is short, extend it on the bench without disturbing the input joints.
On the bench, remove the caps from the head power pair. Trim the pair at the mark.
Take the body half of the head light connector (E10) from {step:head-harness}. Solder its +5 V and GND wires to the matching head power pair wires.
Solder its DATA wire to the outgoing DATA wire after light 5.
Insulate each joint separately. Insulate the two unused outgoing power wires after light 5 separately.
With the meter in continuity mode, check that the +5 V contacts of both body halves on the strand connect.
Check the two GND contacts the same way. Check that +5 V does not reach GND.
steps.check: Lights 0 to 5 are cut from INPUT. The input harness, with the data resistor (R2), is still attached. The head light connector’s body half is soldered on and +5 V does not reach GND.

panels.caption: The first six pebbles from INPUT, with the cut point after the sixth.

panels.title: Test-route the two light cables
panels.caption: The input harness at the strand input, with the head power pair.

panels.title: Solder the head light connector’s body half
panels.caption: The output end after light 5, with DATA continuing to the head light connector.

steps.title: Fit the six body lights
actions: Stand the base on its feet. Find the three side slots on the robot-right face of the rear upright (P02).
Slide an M3 nut into the middle slot until it stops. Load the upper slot the same way.
Slide an M3 nut into each of the three side slots on the robot-left face of the front upright.
At the lower slot, hold a front body-light bracket (P11) on the upright, countersunk hole facing forward. Put an M3×10 countersunk screw through it into the nut.
Fit the second P11 at the upper slot the same way. Fit the body wire guide (P13) at the middle slot. Tighten all three screws.
If a screw does not catch, check that its nut is fully in the slot.
Turn the rear body-light bracket (P12) so both pads face forward. They angle 10° outward.
Hold it on the back of the rear upright, over the middle nut. Line up the holes.
Tape it to the upright with low-tack tape.
Place a pebble on each of the six pads, LED facing away from the pad.
At each pebble, pass two 2.5 mm cable ties (C07) through the pad slots. Put one on each side of the resin.
Close each tie gently around the wire. Keep both ties off the resin and the LED.
Leave the wire between pebbles, about 100 mm, in loose loops. Do not pull it tight, stretch it or fold it sharply.
steps.check: Four lights face forward and the two rear lights angle forward. No tie crosses an LED or resin body.
steps.note: The backpack carrier screws hold P12 and use the two rear upright nuts in {step:backpack-carrier}.

panels.caption: The rear upright from behind, with the middle (1) and upper (2) nut positions.

panels.title: Load the three front upright nuts
Fasten the front brackets and wire guide
panels.caption: Both uprights with every body-light bracket fitted, front at the lower right.

panels.title: Tape the rear body-light bracket in place
Tie a pebble to each pad
panels.caption: One pad with its pebble, and a tie on each side of the resin.

panels.title: Leave loose loops between the lights

steps.title: Wrap the body diffuser
actions: Slide an M3 nut into the lower side slot on the robot-right face of the rear upright.
Run the three servo cables and the body half of the body light connector down the frame. Pass them through the central opening into the base.
Keep them clear of the rear seam and of sharp edges.
Cut the body foam (C04) from the body foam template: 224.8 × 114.3 mm, from 4 mm foam. Cut it slightly long.
Cut the two knife slits marked on the template, one to each shoulder. Remove no foam.
Test-fit the foam between the two foam collars (P01), front center at the front upright. Trim both ends to a 2 mm gap at the rear upright. Keep the edge notches full size.
Hold a rear seam backing (P09) on the back of the rear upright, over the upper nut. Line up the holes. Tape it there with low-tack tape.
Wrap the foam again, over the taped backing. Leave both shoulder horn seats clear.
Lift the foam edges at the lower nut. Slide the other P09 behind them. Line up its hole with the upright’s hole.
With one hand, press a rear seam cover (P10) over the seam there, holding P09 against the upright. With the other, drive an M3×16 screw through P10 and P09 into the nut and tighten it.
Fit the other two P10 covers over the seam at the middle and upper nuts. The rear body-light bracket (P12) backs the middle one.
steps.check: The foam sits in both collars without stretching. Its ends meet at the rear seam, and the lower cover is screwed.
steps.note: The backpack carrier screws hold the middle and upper covers in {step:backpack-carrier}.

panels.title: Load the lower rear seam nut
Run the cables down to the base
Cut the foam and trim it to fit
Wrap the foam
panels.caption: The wrapped body from the rear, with the seam covers drawn apart from the seam.

steps.title: Prepare the upper arms
actions: Lay the robot-left upper arm (AR01) with its inner round recess facing up. Slide an M2 nut into each side channel until it stops.
Seat a drilled servo horn (E02) in the recess, splined hub up. Drive an M2×6 screw through each drilled hole into its nut.
If a screw does not catch, push its nut further into the channel.
Fit the other horn to the robot-right upper arm (AR04) the same way, with two M2×6 screws and nuts.
steps.check: Both horns sit flat in their recesses, splined hub up, and each horn’s center hole is clear.

panels.caption: The same two views for the robot-right upper arm.

steps.title: Build the elbows
actions: Slide the tongue of the robot-left forearm (AR02) between the fork cheeks of the robot-left upper arm (AR01). Line up the holes.
From the outer side, push an M3×14 screw through the fork and tongue. Put an M3 nut in the pocket on the inner cheek.
Hold the nut in its pocket with a fingertip. Turn the screw until it catches.
Tighten the screw until the elbow holds a pose but still bends smoothly by hand through 0–70°.
Build the robot-right elbow the same way, from the robot-right upper arm (AR04) and forearm (AR05).
steps.check: Both elbows hold a pose and bend by hand without binding. Neither fork is cracked.
steps.note: You adjust the elbow stiffness at this screw in {step:arm-service}.

panels.caption: The robot-left elbow, with its screw and nut drawn out of the fork.

panels.title: Set the stiffness and build the robot-right elbow

safety.text: Overtightening squeezes the fork cheeks together. The fork can crack. Stop tightening once the elbow holds a pose.

steps.title: Fit the hands and test-fit the shoulder covers
actions: Let the four disc magnets (C08), 3/16 × 1/16 inch, snap together into one column. Add a fifth if you fit the optional pointing hand.
Slide the magnets off the top one at a time. Mark the top face of the first two A. Turn each of the rest over. Mark its top face B.
Each A face now attracts each B face. The A faces go out of the forearms, and the B faces out of the hands.
Put a small amount of two-part epoxy (C09) in the magnet seat of the robot-left forearm (AR02). Keep it off the wrist socket walls and end stops.
Press in an A magnet, A face out. Glue an A magnet into the robot-right forearm (AR05) the same way.
Glue a B magnet into the wrist peg of the robot-left relaxed hand (AR03) the same way, B face out. Keep epoxy off the outside of the peg.
Do the same for the robot-right relaxed hand (AR06). The optional robot-left pointing hand (AR07) replaces AR03. It takes the fifth magnet, also B face out.
Lay the arms and hands apart, so the magnets cannot pull each other out. Let the epoxy cure for the time on its label.
Push AR03 into the AR02 wrist socket, pressing on the palm. Turn it to a pose. Fit AR06 into AR05 the same way.
Each hand sits fully in its socket. The magnet holds it on, and friction holds its angle.
Slide the robot-left shoulder cover (AR08) onto the outer face of the robot-left upper arm (AR01). Pull it off again.
Test-fit the robot-right shoulder cover (AR09) on the robot-right upper arm (AR04) the same way.
Each cover slides fully on and pulls off by hand. The center screws go in through this face in {step:shelf-arms}.
steps.check: Each hand holds its pose on its forearm. Both shoulder covers fit their upper arms and are off again.

panels.caption: Above, the A magnet over the forearm seat. Below, a cutaway of the seated magnet.

panels.caption: Above, the B magnet under the hand seat. Below, a cutaway of the seated magnet.

panels.caption: The robot-left relaxed hand above the robot-left forearm’s wrist socket.

panels.caption: The robot-left shoulder cover sliding onto the upper arm.

steps.title: Fit the backpack carrier
actions: Hold the curved backpack carrier (P34) against the middle and upper rear seam covers (P10), hollow side in. Line up its two center holes with theirs.
With the other hand, drive an M3×18 screw through each center hole into its rear upright nut. Tighten both evenly.
If a screw does not catch, line up the holes in the cover and backing behind it.
steps.check: Each screw holds the carrier, a seam cover and a backing. The rear body-light bracket (P12) backs the middle cover, and a rear seam backing (P09) the top one. The carrier follows the body curve.
steps.note: You loaded the two rear upright nuts in {step:body-lights}.

panels.caption: The rear upright from behind, foam hidden, with the carrier, seam covers and backings drawn apart.

steps.title: Build and attach the backpack
actions: Lay the backpack shell (P35) rear face down. The rear face has the four counterbored screw holes.
Slide a backpack tank (P36) through the two rings at each side, dome end toward the rolled top edge.
Turn each tank until the hole in its wall lines up under the hole in the tab above it.
Drop an M3×8 screw into one tab hole, so its tip enters the tank.
Through the tank’s open end, hold an M3 nut in the pocket under the screw tip with fine pliers. Tighten the screw into it. Fasten the other tank the same way.
If a screw does not catch, check that the nut sits flat in its pocket.
Push a nozzle plug (P37) into the open end of each tank. It closes the tank nut access. Fit the backpack top band (P40) over the middle of the rolled top edge.
Fit the robot-left backpack elbow (P38): lower pin into its tank’s dome hole, side pin into the rolled top edge. Fit the robot-right elbow (P39) the same way.
Each part seats without force, and both tank screws can still be reached.
Take off the plugs, elbows and top band. Glue each back in place with a small amount of two-part epoxy (C09).
Let the epoxy cure for the time on its label.
Stand behind the robot. Slide an M3 nut into each of the four side channels of the backpack carrier (P34). Push each in until it stops.
Hold the backpack on the carrier, belt docks at the bottom. Line up its four rear holes with the carrier nuts.
With the other hand, drive an M3×12 screw through each hole into its nut. Keep the two lower belt docks clear.
If a screw does not catch, push its nut further into the channel.
steps.check: The tanks, plugs, elbows and top band are secure. The shell comes off backward once its four screws are removed.

panels.caption: A cutaway of one tank joint: the screw in the shell tab and the nut pocket inside the tank.

panels.title: Test-fit the plugs, elbows and top band
panels.caption: The backpack from behind, with the plugs, elbows and top band drawn out of place.

panels.title: Glue the plugs, elbows and top band
Load the four carrier nuts
panels.caption: The carrier on its own, with a nut beside each side channel.

panels.title: Screw the backpack to the carrier
panels.caption: The finished backpack drawn back from the carrier, with its four screws.

steps.title: Assemble the belt
actions: Lay the seven belt links flat in a U, as pictured from above. Keep the open end away from you.
Put the robot-left rear belt link (B01) at the right end. Add two front belt links (B02), the belt buckle (B03), two more B02 and the robot-right rear belt link (B04).
Face the buckle frame outward.
Nest each link’s knuckle in the next link’s fork. Push a belt pin (B09) down through each joint, head up. The head has three small notches.
Six pins join the seven links.
Bring the belt around the body from the front. Nest the end of each rear link between the tabs of a lower belt dock on the backpack shell (P35).
Push the last two B09 pins down through the docks.
Every joint pivots, and each pin head sits slightly below the top edge.
steps.check: Every belt joint pivots without cracking. Each rear joint opens when its pin is pushed up from below with a spare pin. The rear link must be supported then, so its side band does not bend.

steps.title: Connect the three servo cables
actions: Support the robot in its stand. Bring the BASE→BODY lighting lead and three separately labeled servo cables through the smooth central opening into the enclosure. Keep each cable identifiable; connect LEFT to the shown ports.
Connect RIGHT, then gently pull-check both WAGO wires and its signal wire.
Connect the head servo. Keep its cable distinct from the separate HEAD lighting plug.
